subject: Request: Subprocessor mapping and EU transit clarification
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finservco.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinServCo Security <security@finservco.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:17:00 +0000
Subject: Subprocessor mapping + transit question

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the recent demo — FinServCo is preparing our procurement package and we need one final clarification before we move to legal review. Could you send an updated subprocessor roster and a simple data-flow note indicating whether any EU-customer production data would transit through US-based control planes or service endpoints (even if at-rest/processing remains in EU)?

Specifically: 
- A current matrix of subprocessors (name, purpose, primary region of processing)
- Any control plane or logging endpoints that are hosted outside the EU and could carry metadata or telemetry
- Confirmation of whether we can require EU-only routing for our tenant under the DPA amendment

We have a short window — would appreciate the docs and a proposed timeline for contract amendment.

Best,
Elena
Elena Rossi
Data Protection Officer, FinServCo
elena.rossi@finservco.com

---
Note: we will also need SOC 2 evidence as part of the package; please advise if that is already available via your security portal.

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finservco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 14:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor mapping + transit question

Elena — thanks for the note and the clear list. Attaching our current subprocessor matrix and the latest DPA (v3) for your review. High level answers below: 

- Matrix: see attached subprocessor_matrix_20261210.xlsx (columns: vendor, purpose, region, data_types, legal_basis).
- Transit: For EU-hosted tenants we route inference and embeddings traffic to EU regions by default. However, one new vendor (EdgeStream CDN) uses an EU data plane for content but relies on a US-based control plane for configuration/telemetry. That means metadata (service logs, control signals) could briefly route via the vendor's US control plane, not production customer payloads.
- EU-only routing: We can offer contractual routing constraints in the DPA amendment and operationalise them for production workloads, with Service Level constraints. Laura from Legal will confirm the precise language; cc'd.

SOC 2: We publish the report to customers under NDA; we can share an encrypted copy via the security portal link once you confirm the HubSpot record.

Next steps suggested: 
1) Legal review of EdgeStream's control plane flow and DPA amendment language (Laura)
2) Sign DPA amendment (DocuSign) after review
3) Operational verification: we will run a short test to show no customer payload leaves EU before cutover

Attachments: subprocessor_matrix_20261210.xlsx, redwood-dpa-v3.pdf

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales, EMEA — Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai
+44 20 7000 5555

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@finservco.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor mapping + transit question

Thanks Priya / Elena — looping in Legal to do a quick pass on the EdgeStream control plane note and to confirm whether the DPA amendment text we proposed covers EU-only routing requirements.

Laura — quick context: FinServCo is evaluating Redwood for production inference. They require confirmation that production payloads remain in EU and want any control-plane metadata minimised or contractually restricted. Priya attached the matrix and DPA. I also added a lightweight data-flow diagram (see attached) that maps where logs/telemetry could traverse. Can Legal confirm whether the proposed amendment + SCCs are sufficient or whether we need a subprocessors-specific rider?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: data_flow_diagram.png

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 15:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor mapping + transit question — Legal response and next steps

Elena / team — apologies for the slight delay. We reviewed the attached matrix and the EdgeStream technical notes. Summary and proposed path forward below: 

1) EdgeStream: Approved with safeguards. The vendor stores and serves content from EU-hosted edge nodes; the control plane is in the US. We recommend an amendment clause that: 
   - Prohibits processing of customer payloads outside the EU for EU accounts;
   - Limits control-plane telemetry to metadata only and requires pseudonymisation where feasible;
   - Requires timely notice of any subprocessor changes and a right to object.

2) DPA amendment: We will prepare an amendment draft that incorporates the routing constraint and adds a subprocessor notification schedule (30 days). We will route the amendment for signature via DocuSign and include SCCs where applicable.

3) SOC 2: We can provide a copy under NDA via the security portal; Priya will share the portal link in HubSpot.

DocuSign link (DPA amendment draft): https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABC123456789
HubSpot record for package: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/987654/record/FS-4521

If this approach sounds good, we’ll push the amendment to DocuSign today and provide an operational verification checklist for the controlled rollout.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0132
